def factor_asymmetry_reversal(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    # Primary reversal with asymmetry (from parent)
    ret = df_copy["close"] / df_copy["close"].shift(1) - 1
    pos_mask = ret > 0
    neg_mask = ret < 0
    up_vol = (ret.where(pos_mask, 0.0) ** 2).rolling(60, min_periods=30).mean() ** 0.5
    down_vol = (ret.where(neg_mask, 0.0) ** 2).rolling(60, min_periods=30).mean() ** 0.5
    asym = (down_vol - up_vol) / (down_vol + up_vol).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    asym_smooth = asym.ewm(span=10).mean()
    range_ = df_copy["high"] - df_copy["low"]
    loc = (df_copy["close"] - df_copy["low"]) / range_.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    reversal_raw = (0.5 - loc) * range_ / df_copy["close"]
    scale_asym = 1.0 + 0.5 * asym_smooth
    factor = reversal_raw * scale_asym
    # Smooth with EMA to reduce noise (mutation)
    factor = factor.ewm(span=3).mean()
    df_copy["factor_asymmetry_reversal"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_asymmetry_reversal"]
description: This mutation removes the volume climax modifier from the parent, which was causing payoff gate failure, and instead adds a short EMA smoothing (span=3) to the raw asymmetry-amplified reversal signal. The core economic mechanism remains: intraday location (close-low)/(high-low) captures closing position; low location suggests upward reversal, amplified when downside volatility exceeds upside volatility (asym>0). The EMA reduces noise while preserving the mean-reversion signal, aiming to improve IC and ICIR stability.
